A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same prime-attention research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments, initialization and sparsity ablations, runtime measurements, and attention-map analyses in Section 7 and Appendices F–H.

after.justification: v2 retains original forecasting experiments and adds parameter controls, key/value ablations, and repeated-run results in Section 6 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The core pair-specific key/value modulation and MLP primer construction are retained. However, v2 Section 4 describes instantaneous correlation as a simple dot product, while v1 Appendix F.1 and retained v2 Appendix E.1 specify Pearson correlation, rolling standard deviation, and rank transformations. The PDFs therefore do not resolve whether this computation actually changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 11 forecasting datasets and retain the same long-term and short-term task coverage. The additional ECL/Traffic comparisons, attention maps, and component controls use already represented datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 2 and 8 add DIFF Transformer, LIFT, and Autoformer comparisons on the already evaluated ECL and Traffic datasets; v1 reported these comparators only on ETTh1, ETTh2, Exchange, and Weather. The original comparisons remain, and v2 supplies no LagTS results for the added rows.

E3.justification: The existing splits, forecasting horizons, metrics, and listed training configurations remain unchanged. New controls compare eight versus nine attention heads while increasing model width to preserve per-head dimensions, and test modulation of keys alone, values alone, or both (v2 Section 6.4 and Appendix E.5).

E4.justification: v2 adds substantive controls addressing whether gains follow from extra attention capacity and whether both key and value modulation are necessary. It also adds ECL attention-map analysis. Existing sparsity, initialization, sequence-length, and runtime analyses remain; the Solar analysis is additionally presented in the main text.

E5.justification: v1 does not report repeated-run counts or experimental uncertainty. v2 Appendix A.2 states that results average five randomly seeded runs, and Appendix A.5/Table 6 reports means and standard deviations across five datasets and four horizons. This establishes new reporting, not a demonstrated increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for the head-capacity control, key/value ablation, stability study, ECL attention maps, and expanded baseline comparisons. For example, Table 7 reports Weather MSE of 0.174 for either single-component modulation versus 0.170 for both. Retained ETTh2 scores also change: prime iTransformer's average MSE/MAE shifts from 0.379/0.405 to 0.377/0.404. Most other original benchmark values and all original plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix C's auxiliary graph definitions, message-passing equations, sparse prime-GAT formulation, and associated O(|E| × dmodel) argument are omitted. The central static/dynamic definitions, universal-approximation proof, and gradient derivations remain substantively unchanged. Relabeling the main theorems as propositions is editorial.

C1.justification: The dynamic-relational-learning contribution and headline claims of up to 6.5% forecasting improvement and 40% shorter inputs remain. v2's introduction adds the concrete claim of approximately 1.5% parameter overhead, extending the earlier asymptotic-complexity argument with a parameter-efficiency claim.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies attention maps as correlational rather than causal evidence and labels its Solar mechanism explanation speculative. It interprets the new capacity control as evidence against gains arising simply from extra parameters. Conversely, the earlier high-dimensional memory warning is replaced with a more favorable applicability statement.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link and discloses primer computation timing, MLP parameter sharing, and approximately 1.5% parameter overhead. Existing hardware and hyperparameter tables remain. Detailed graph-adaptation instructions are removed despite retention of the GAT runtime experiment, and the new correlation description conflicts with the retained appendix.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion or citations covering SDformer, gated attention, two Lee–Clark works, and additional universal-approximation research. References supporting the removed graph appendix, including expander and Cayley graph propagation, disappear. The central positioning of pair-specific modulation against static relational learning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are condensed, related work gains subheadings and absorbs the former attention-sharpening section, and several headings and theorem labels change. An impact statement is added. Much of the existing methodological, theoretical, and appendix prose is retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text and references, substantially changing table placement and typography. It adds three tables and ECL attention-map displays, redisplays Solar maps in the main text, and enlarges forecasting visualizations onto separate pages. Original plotted content is otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The added capacity and key/value controls, five-run variability reporting, code-access information, and explicit caution about causal interpretation strengthen support for the existing contribution. The improvement is limited by conflicting primer-computation descriptions and removal of graph-adaptation details needed to understand the retained GAT experiment. These tradeoffs support a modest net quality improvement.
